source: the agent session's own event log (tool.execution_start/complete, external_tool.requested/completed, system.notification, assistant.turn_start and assistant.message events); only tool names, timestamps and a short note were copied

semantics.kind: process = the tool starts an operating-system process (PowerShell, ripgrep); in_process = it runs inside the CLI process (file views and edits, SQL, waiting on a shell)
semantics.span: interval = the process runs between start_utc and end_utc (synchronous commands); instants = only the start and end are treated as activity (calls that wait, and asynchronous launches)
semantics.exit_utc: exit of an asynchronous shell, only where the runtime delivered a completion notification
semantics.model_turns: from the start of a model request to the end of its last streamed message, per turn; includes network latency

limitations: Only tool-call boundaries and model-response intervals are recorded; the CPU used by the agent runtime, the desktop app (rendering, streaming) and the model client is not attributed to calls.
The process/in-process split is assumed from the tool name: powershell, grep, glob and stop_powershell are taken to start operating-system processes, all other tools to run inside the CLI process.
Asynchronous shells have an exit instant only where a completion notification exists.
Timestamps come from the CLI's event log on the same host clock as the monitor.
Activity of the user, other applications and other app sessions is not recorded here.
